findings.title: retryCount delete branch is not scoped to SMS and cannot use the existing index
findings.body:
The `deleteMany` OR has a second branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. The SMS cron will therefore delete EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders with `retryCount > 1`. Today only this handler increments the counter, but any other reminder cron that adopts the new column would have its reminders deleted by the SMS cron, which is surprising cross-method data loss.

The branch is also unindexed. `retryCount` has no index, and the OR stops Postgres from relying on `@@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate])`. This is likely to become a sequential scan of the whole WorkflowReminder table (all methods, all history) on every cron run.

Fix: add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and probably `scheduled: false`) to the second branch.

findings.title: Transient failures permanently delete reminders after two cron runs
findings.body:
The catch block increments `retryCount` for any exception in the try body. That includes transient errors such as Twilio 5xx or 429 rate limits, network timeouts, the `prisma.profile.findFirst` or `getBookerBaseUrl` calls, and template rendering. It also includes the `scheduled: true` update failing after Twilio already accepted the message.

After two failures the row is deleted on the next run. Previously the reminder would be retried until its scheduled date (up to 7 days out). Now a short Twilio or DB outage spanning two cron invocations silently and permanently drops every SMS reminder processed during it.

If the post-schedule update is what failed, the reminder is retried and deleted while a Twilio message is already queued. That causes duplicate sends, and the `referenceId` needed to cancel the queued message is lost.

Only known-permanent errors (e.g. Twilio invalid-number error codes) should count toward deletion, or the retry budget should be larger or time-based.

findings.title: SMS-locked users/teams have their reminders deleted
findings.body:
`twilio.scheduleSMS` returns `undefined`, not an error, when the user or team has `smsLockState === LOCKED`. This new `else` branch treats that as a failed attempt and increments `retryCount`, so after two cron runs every pending SMS reminder for that account is deleted.

Previously these reminders stayed unscheduled and would be sent if an admin unlocked the account, for example after a false-positive abuse lock. Now unlocking does not restore them and attendees silently get no reminders.

The locked case should be distinguished from a real scheduling failure.

findings.title: Failure inside the catch handler aborts the whole cron run
findings.body:
The catch block now awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` before logging. If that update throws, the exception escapes the `for` loop and the handler. This happens for example when the original error was a DB connectivity problem, or when the row was deleted concurrently (e.g. a booking cancellation), which makes Prisma throw `P2025`.

All remaining reminders in the batch are then skipped, the endpoint returns 500, and the original error is never logged. Before this PR the catch only logged, so one bad reminder could not stop the rest.

Wrap the counter update in its own try/catch, or log first and ignore update failures.

findings.title: Reminders with no recipient or empty message are still retried indefinitely
findings.body: The PR's goal is to stop endlessly re-processing reminders that can never be sent. However, when `sendTo` is null (e.g. `smsReminderNumber` missing) or the rendered message is empty, the `if` at this line is skipped. Neither branch increments `retryCount`, so these reminders are still re-fetched and fully re-processed on every cron run until their scheduled date. That includes the profile lookup, booker-URL resolution and template rendering. These permanently unsendable cases are arguably the ones that most need the retry cap.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behavior
findings.body: The PR adds behavior that deletes user-facing reminders, but no tests cover it. Cases worth testing: incrementing `retryCount` on a falsy `scheduleSMS` result and on thrown errors, deleting reminders with `retryCount > 1`, leaving reminders of other methods untouched, and not deleting on success. Given the data-loss risk if the conditions are wrong, these should be covered.
